newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower after string of records.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower after string of records.

text.p: After a string of record closes last week, Swiss shares ended more than one percent lower, dragged down by losses in index-heavyweight shares.
Dealers said Wall Street's early weakness and the fall in the dollar put blue-chip stocks such as Novartis, Roche and Nestle under pressure.
Volume was moderate as investors were cautious before the outcome of today's meeting by U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC).
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) slid 76.5 points, or 1.48 percent, to 5,081.0 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 41.63 points to 3,214.28 points.
Bourse volume was at 1.96 billion Swiss francs.
One dealer said profit taking was nothing unusual after last week's record run. He added that markets are closely following the Fed's FOMC meeting.
"But even the Fed were to raise interest rates, it would not be entirely negative, because it would help the dollar," he said.
Most-traded Novartis registered shares fell 38 francs to 1,973 and Roche certificates were down 290 francs to 13,205. Nestle lost 39 francs to 1,818.
Swiss Re, CS Group and Elektrowatt were among the few blue-chip winners.
Swiss Re shares were up 10 francs to 1,834. The company said it expected a rise in 1997 net premiums of 20 to 25 percent.

Elektrowatt, in which CS Group has a stake of 44.9 percent, profited from a media report saying the spin-off of Elektrowatt's energy business may take place without the expected tax payment of 150 million francs.
A CS Group spokesman said the article was basically correct.
CS Group was up 1.50 francs to 173.50 while Elektrowatt soared seven francs to 533.
